editorial.summary: Episode 038 has no outside guest. David Choe, Asa Akira, Critter, Valentin (Yacuzzi Boy), and Bobby Namba record a fourth consecutive show while openly sleep-deprived. Merchandise planning and body commentary lead into David's account of a commercial trip to Switzerland for Fin Bec winery, following Mode 2 and REVOK. Fees, travel, wine, and a bodyguard request remain his attributed account. Critter explains the childhood origin of his nickname and discusses stuttering; private family members remain unindexed, and the room's causal theories are not medical guidance. A long discussion of fighting includes David's coercive judo joke, descriptions of choking and kicking people, and Asa's account of asking Chuck Liddell to choke her unconscious on a Bubba the Love Sponge broadcast. None is safety instruction. Critter's defense-of-women story turns into a debate over retaliatory violence. Valentin recounts striking a former partner after she struck him; Asa recounts a moving-car fight during a former marriage and opioid-using period. Both private partners remain unidentified and the accounts remain unverified first-person testimony. David then narrates a two-year relationship with a former Power Rangers performer who is identifiable from contextual clues. The editorial record deliberately does not name her. His account combines poverty, shoplifting, gambling, emotional and physical abuse, a dangerous exit from a moving car, disputed sexual allegations, revenge fantasies, and the belief that suffering produced ambition. That retrospective theory is not causal psychology and does not excuse violence or crime. A San Diego Comic-Con confrontation introduces Joe Hahn of Linkin Park. This leads to the episode's strongest work-history passage: David says he created the art for *Collision Course*, the Jay-Z/Linkin Park collaboration, then disputed downstream advertising uses. He says Sean Parker rejected Warner representatives during Facebook fundraising because of the dispute, and that Joe Hahn later helped after learning about it. Those rights, payment, and investment claims are useful but remain attributed. Pat Tenore of RVCA and Jim Lee connect the two men. Asa recalls meeting Bobby Lee while she was under eighteen and attributes a sexualized remark to him; the record preserves the troubling age context without treating private dialogue as verified. The final hour shifts from fighting to jealousy. Bobby describes old friends approaching him with a film-business proposal; David admits possessiveness and a wish to curate Bobby's social world. Quiet C/Carol, an imagined proposal, and a three-month bachelor party are plans and jokes, not evidence of an engagement. Bobby's private friends remain unindexed. David closes with an account of excluding a private gallery worker after complaints of inappropriate conduct; the person and allegation remain outside searchable metadata. Trivia is deferred because the show is 'truncated.' All 2,422 spoken segments survive cleaning; three empty zero-duration artifacts are removed.
